Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and attached artifacts. I've copied Ben (Solutions) for technical follow-up and Grace (Reliability) for runbook confirmation.

Summary answers (Hosted API / Dedicated):
- RTO: 60s token-stream preservation for active sessions; end-to-end restore for customer workloads typically within 30 minutes (hosted) / 15 minutes (dedicated reserved capacity) for service-level recovery after region failover.
- RPO: Stateless generative requests are designed for eventual consistency; session-level KV cache persists to cross-region replication within 2 minutes for priority tenants (configurable). For Dedicated, RPO for stateful KV can be configured down to ~30s with replication profiles.
- Automated switchover: policy-driven (latency or capacity) with automatic fallback to regional peers; automated detection triggers can initiate traffic reroute within 90 seconds. Manual failover: used for planned maintenance and takes 5–20 minutes depending on the sanity checks and canary validation.
- Data replication: control-plane metadata and audit logs are synchronously replicated to secondary region with 1–5s lag; KV cache replication is async by default with configurable sync windows.

Attachments included: Redwood_BCP_Statement.pdf (high-level commitment), switchover-matrix.csv (timings and steps), runbook-excerpt.txt (sanity checks).

If you need numeric SLAs added to contract language (e.g., < 2m replication for priority data), Ben can provide the exact profile names we recommend.

Laura — quick technical follow-up with the explicit numbers your SRE team asked for. Short answers + reference to the switchover matrix we attached.

1) RTO recommendations (by scenario):
   - Control-plane outage (API gateway auth, orchestration): automated regional failover target = 3 minutes for traffic reroute; full control-plane stabilization and cached state reconciliation within 1 hour.
   - Regional compute failure (GPU hosts): for active streaming sessions we preserve token continuity in 60s windows when prefix caching is enabled; for bulk batch jobs resume on secondary with job retry semantics (typical restart < 20 minutes).

2) RPO recommendations and configurable profiles:
   - Bronze (default hosted): async KV replication, target RPO = 2 minutes for session info, best-effort for larger artifacts.
   - Silver (recommended for production): near-sync window, target RPO = 30 seconds for KV and session checkpoints.
   - Gold (Dedicated enterprise): active-active replication for customer data, target RPO <= 5 seconds (requires reserved replication profile & network config).

3) Automated vs manual switchover behavior:
   - Automated: health checks + latency/failure thresholds trigger route policy. Canary traffic is first sent to secondary for 60s smoke test; if green, we shift primary traffic in stages. Automated path aims to reduce human intervention but still sends notices to oncall.
   - Manual: operator-initiated with a rollback window. Used for DR rehearsals. Manual takes longer due to safety gates (5–20 minutes).

4) Evidence for RFP: switchover-matrix.csv contains step-by-step timings. runbook-excerpt.txt includes the canary test checklist and escalation tree. Redwood_BCP_Statement.pdf is a signed engineering-level commitment (non-contractual). We can convert the Gold profile to contractual SLA language if needed.

Let me know if you want a short recorded walkthrough of a simulated switchover — I can share a timed demo clip.

- Ben

Hi Laura — adding operational clarifications from the runbook side. A couple of practical notes your SREs usually ask about:

- Canary window: we run a 60s smoke test with 1% of production traffic (isolated tenant routing) then expand to 10% for 5 minutes before full cutover. Observability thresholds include token drop rate, response latency P95, and model-quality signals (difference from baseline).
- Circuit breakers: if any of the three core thresholds fail during canary, an automatic rollback to primary is executed and oncall is paged.
- Failback process: after incident resolution we validate state reconciliation (KV deltas < configured threshold) before traffic is moved back. This typically adds 10–30 minutes to full restoration time.

Operational attachments referenced in the runbook excerpt:
- escalation-tree (included in runbook-excerpt.txt)
- sanity-check scripts (internal link: https://redwood-internal.company/runbooks/region-switchover-v2)

We also run quarterly DR rehearsals for Dedicated customers who opt into our DR program; we can provide a schedule and past rehearsal notes under NDA.
